pr_title: resolved: fixes when trying to serialize overly long DNS names
pr_body:
A comprehensive fix for #33671

Fixes: #33671 
Fixes: #34416
pr_comments: The fuzz target fails because of https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/34416

As for compression and appending things to packets that stuff is barely tested. The fuzz targets barely poke that part so ideally it would be great to extend `fuzz-dns-packet` to make sure that packets can survive a round-trip in resolved. Currently it just parses packets without trying to go over them and adding whatever it has parsed to a new packet to make sure that it's all consistent.
Force pushed a new version that also fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/34416. Let's see if this passes CI

issue_context.title: resolved accepts resource records with overly long domain names
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

00f546e25e8e46e5e289e1f2fc2ed3dcc6999223

### Used distribution

Fedora 40

### Linux kernel version used

Linux version 6.10.9-200.fc40.x86_64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

None

### Component

systemd-resolved

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

resolved should probably reject overly large domain names.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

resolved accepts resource records with overly large domain names in various places. For example they can be stuffed into its mDNS cache:
```sh
$ resolvectl show-cache
Scope protocol=mdns family=AF_INET ifindex=3 ifname=eth1
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa 192.168.1.1
```
```sh
$ resolvectl show-cache --json pretty
...
                                                "rr" : {
                                                        "key" : {
                                                                "class" : 1,
                                                                "type" : 1,
                                                                "name" : "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
aaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.local"
                                                        },
                                                        "address" : [
                                                                192,
                                                                168,
                                                                1,
                                                                1
                                                        ]
                                                },
```

The fuzz target started failing in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/34391 because of that.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

With https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/33806 it can be injected locally too:
```sh
printf '\x00\x00\x84\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa?aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa\x05local\x00\x00\x01\x80\x01\x00\x00\x00x\x00\x04\xc0\xa8\x01\x01' | ncat -u 224.0.0.251 5353
```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
